source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 164: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer: Use the same checkpoint, tokenizer, request trace and output-length mix, decoding, server/runtime, scheduler, hardware, drivers, power and thermal envelope in both arms; change only weight precision and hold activation and KV-cache precision fixed. Record bit width, group size, scales, outlier policy, calibration data and provenance, held-out split, kernel support and fallback path. Test the falsifiable hypothesis for variant 164: at each predeclared concurrency, quantization reduces fully loaded cost per successful output token by a stated target while held-out quality, safety, correctness, TTFT and TPOT gates pass; reject the claim if a hard gate fails or the confidence interval cannot support the target. After equal warm-up and compilation, run repeated randomized interleaved paired baseline/treatment trials, with disjoint calibration and held-out workloads and predeclared sample size, scoring, stopping rule and confidence-interval method. Measure quality, safety, correctness, peak memory (GiB), TTFT and TPOT (ms/token), throughput (tokens/s), concurrency, utilization, p50/p95/p99, errors, retries, timeouts, OOMs, kernel fallbacks and cleanup failures, all with denominators. Match or stratify prompt length, batch shape, cache state, placement, kernel route and thermal state; distinguish measurements from estimates and include host, accelerator, energy and operational costs. Use only an authorized bounded canary with baseline capacity, redacted traces, tested rollback and stop conditions for quality, safety, correctness or SLO regressions.

Kernel fallback, batching, cache state, placement and thermal throttling can confound latency and throughput.
Missing denominators or incomplete cost accounting can invalidate savings; traces may contain sensitive data.
